source.quote: Specifically, three of Elwin's most profitable rares. Thoros Lightfingers, Mother Fang, and Fedfennel. Now, you might be asking, why these three? There are about seven rare spawns in Elwin after all, but these ones in particular, they have loot worth farming. Let's start with Thoros. He's got two drops for hunting. The fingerless gloves and a little bit more rare, the thugish shield. The gloves drop around 3% and the shield just 1% according to Wowhead. These items have value because of transmogriification or transmog. This is a system in Modern WoW that lets players change the appearance of their gear to match anything they've collected across their account. Some appearances are common and they're shared across a dozen items, but others are totally unique. The thuggish shield, for example, is a one-of-a-kind design.

source.quote: Surrounded by a small troop of NLES, this mini boss doesn't look like much, but he's holding something sharp. You see, we're farming him for one thing. The Pale Skinner, a one-handed sword with a 1.7% drop chance and a history that makes it goldbound worthy. For starters, he was actually removed from the game for a while, completely unobtainable before being readded in patch 8.0.1. Now, that's already enough to get some collectors interested, and the appearance is shared only with one other weapon, the Blackwater Cutless from Deadmines. It's got that classic pirate schwashbuckler vibe. A perfect finishing piece for anyone rocking a sea dog transmog. Now, back in the day, the pale Skinner actually had a special feature. It counted as a skinning knife. Sadly, that function is gone, but the value remains. The auction house pricing puts it at an average of around 127,000 gold.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/002 - Can I Farm 265,000 Gold To Escape Elwynn？ - Goldbound Episode 2.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Of course, players looking purely for the appearance might simply just go run dead mines for the Blackwater version. But if you're a collector or you want the original, the sword still holds some serious value. Now, this isn't something you'd expect to sell immediately, but if one did sell, that's nearly half a WOW token in one swing. A single drop that could literally change the run. And that's two rares down and one more to go. We moved southwest into the darkest corners of Elwin, the place Jasper Load Mine. And buried within its twisting tunnels is a rare unlike any other. After brushing past a few cobalts who might have some interesting drops of their own, more on that soon, we reached our next mark, Mother Fang, a spider rare tucked deep in the mine and arguably the single most valuable mob in all of Elewin Forest. There's one reason we're down here. The brood mother carropase, a leather chest piece with a6% drop chance and a completely unique appearance. Nothing else in the game looks like it. Because of that rarity, the value is massive, averaging nearly 179,000 gold. One drop from the spider could get us more than halfway to our token goal. Goldilocked did what any self-respecting zone locked rogue would do. We camped hard. We kept precise timers and rotated through spawn points.

source.quote: Definitely below drop rate, but a massive W nonetheless. We'll be posting this one up as well. These items are ultra rare, and the sellrough rates reflect that as well. According to Trade Skill Master, items like these sell less than 0.05 times per day. So, in plain terms, they really don't move fast. But that's the game with Transmog. You stock the shelves, you build the inventory, and you keep them posted on the auction house. Because when you've got 100 rare items posted, even a 1% sale rate means that something sells every couple of days. So, no, we're not banking on these transmogong items alone to buy our way out of Elwin, but it's a foundation and a passive pipeline. But I wasn't ready to just sit in Storwind waiting for sales. Jasper Load Mine has more to offer. There's something a little more primal, the grind. There's spiders, there's cobalts, and there's copper ore.

And if a collector's using the auction to fill up their missing wardrobe slots, we might just get lucky. But there's something a little bit more consistent. The cobalt mining mallet. This one drops fairly often from the cobalts and jasper load. It shares its appearance with the Rock Shard Club and Cotto Mallet, so it's not exclusive. It has a solid average list price of over a,000 gold. Although the average sale price is only 37 gold, but more importantly, it is a 4% average daily sale rate. It's not going to find a WOW token on its own, but posting a few of these can definitely move the needle if we sell a few for a couple hundred gold. source.quote: It's passive farming, and every little bit helps chip away at that Wow token toll. So, as we continue working toward our WoW token, let's talk a little bit about the journey itself. Right now, we're locked to Elwin Forest with Stormwind serving as our designated major city access mainly for auction house and banking. Now, there is a case to be made that we could farm the stockades, a dungeon located right inside Stormwind, but if I'm being honest, I never intended to exploit Stormwind as a gold farm hub, at least in Elwin. So, we're going to keep things simple. All of our gold for this leg of the challenge is going to be Elwin based. In the future, when we unlock a new zone that has a dungeon entrance within it, we'll absolutely be allowed to run that instance for gold, but it needs to be clearly located within the unlocked zone. That way, we're staying true to the gold bound journey. And speaking of future zones, let's take a look at the map. Since we're in Elewin now, once we purchase a WoW token, we'll spin a randomizer to determine our next unlocked zone. Accessible by foot from where we are. For us, that means Westfall, a classic early leveling zone.

source.quote: We'll be doing a full mailbox clear and/played reveal at the end of this episode. But for now, let's get back to what works. Dual gathering, herbs and ore. It's how we made our first gold, and it's still one of our most reliable methods. The thing is, we've leveled up our method. Goldilocks getting smarter, faster. We've mapped out the zone and found some hidden secrets within Elwin. So, now we're putting our refined gathering route to the test with a few improvements as well. So, let's see what the new meta looks like. First off, as we leveled up, something happened. something very retail. Our mount speed increased automatically. No training, no clicks. Just one day we were zipping through Elwin like a rocket powered pigeon. And that makes a huge difference in farming loops. If you remember from last episode, we discovered a little flip with herbalism where we would gather with the skill, drop herbalism, learn inscription, and mill the herbs down and reset. We found a similar shuffle for coproar. I'll break that down soon. But first, let me show you something even weirder. During one of the many, and I mean many, hours of farming, something strange happened. I was able to gather copper ore while still mounted. At first, I thought it was lag, a fluke. But then it happened again a few minutes later. Turns out if you hover your mount about 1 to 3 ft above the ore, close enough to interact, but far enough that you don't land, it lets you mine without dismounting.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/002 - Can I Farm 265,000 Gold To Escape Elwynn？ - Goldbound Episode 2.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Honestly, not bad. This is a pretty big improvement over our gold gathering rates from the last episode. All without leaving Elwin at all, but this is still just the beginning because it's time to do the Elwin shuffle. First up, we're going to go ahead and smelt all the ore down. This takes a few minutes to process all this ore, but that improves our gold by about one gold per ore. That's decent, but we can still do a lot better. So, the next step is to pivot into engineering. We just have to craft enough rough blasting powder to hit 30 engineering. Then, we simply go back to the trainer and learn a single recipe, the handful of copper bolts. And a quick tip, before you run back to the forge, don't forget to pick up a blacksmith hammer from the trade goods vendor. Otherwise, you'll just be running back again. Not exactly minmax, just minimal brain. From here, it's simple. One copper bar will go into a handful of copper bolts. It takes a while, but these bolts sell for 9 gold each. So, by running this simple two-step process, we more than double the value of our copper ore. And sure, it takes some time, but this is just some AFK time to watch YouTube in the background. And then we move on to the herbs. And this is the exact same herb shuffle that we've run before. Get inscription at level one, just high enough to mill. Pretty easy. And we make sure again we're only milling what we have in our bags even though there's some in our bank that we could technically mill. And for this we're simply just converting the silver leaf paste bloom and earthroot into alabaster pigments so that we can sell. And as simple as that after a few minutes of milling the shuffle is complete. And now we're sitting on 297 copper bolts valued at around 9 gold each. Alongside that we have 266 alabaster pigments. And these go for around 12 gold a piece. And that's a total process value of about 5,865 gold. And the total time to make that just 1 hour and 21 minutes. That's farming and processing, which if you average it out, gives us a gold per hour of 4,300. That's not from flipping, not from rares, just gathering and refining in a starting zone. Now, to be fair, we'll likely sell some of these earth roots and copper ores raw, and we'll probably sell some of the copper ores as copper bars, but we'll try to sell the most of them as the bolts and as the pigments. This is just because the starting zone, the materials here, while they sell, they're still a little bit of slow movers, and sometimes it's better just to offload them quicker. But regardless of the split, this is hands down our most consistent farm so far.
